messages.author: 8451853ac20308a6
messages.subject: invoking lavaan() via lavaan.mi(): Error ... subscript out of bounds
parts:
Hi all,

this is my first post and I hope this is the right place for my problem. I want to estimate a structural equation model with multiply imputed data using lavaan.mi() from the semTools package. The data were previously imputed with the mice package, so I extracted the five imputed data sets with:

imputed<-list()
for(i in 1:5) {
  imputed[[i]] <- complete(imp, i)
}

Then I tried to fit the model:

sem.m3.fit<-lavaan.mi(sem.m3, data=imputed, chi="all", likelihood="wishart", int.ov.free=T,
int.lv.free=F, auto.fix.first=T, auto.fix.single=T, auto.var=T, auto.cov.lv.x=F, auto.cov.y=F, auto.th=T, auto.delta=T)

This leaves me with an error message:

Error in `[<-`(`*tmp*`, rhs, lhs, value = 1) : subscript out of bounds

However, when I fit the model with just one of the imputed data sets,

sem.m3.fit<-lavaan(sem.m3, data=imputed[[1]], likelihood="wishart", int.ov.free=T,
int.lv.free=F, auto.fix.first=T, auto.fix.single=T, auto.var=T, auto.cov.lv.x=F, auto.cov.y=F, auto.th=T, auto.delta=T)

the model is fitted without any error. I varied the arguments in lavaan.mi() that are passed to lavaan() and tried sem.mi() as an alternative - to no avail. Therefore, if I didn't make a mistake, I suspect the problem might be in lavaan.mi() [or the function it wraps, runMI()] rather than lavaan(). Still, as Yves Rosseel also contributes to the semTools package, I suspected this might be the right place to ask for help. So: Can anybody help me out? Thanks in advance.

Christian

Hmmm, this is a bit hard to diagnose without a but more information. There are a couple of things you might try:

1. Does running lavaan work on each imputed data set (you tried with the first but the problem might crop up in another one).
2. When you run lavaan.mi, try setting chi="none" If this works, it will help us pinpoint the issue.
3. If you're willing, posting the code you're using to define the model is always helpful.

Alex

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: invoking lavaan() via lavaan.mi(): Error ... subscript out of bounds
parts:
Okay, I've pinpointed the problem playing with some of my own data. The issue is in the specification of the higher order factors. Currently, when higher order factors are specified using the =~ operator to define the higher order factor kicks back an error (this stems from the specification of the null and saturated models used when computing model fit indices). I'll put this on the list of issues to fix. 

Fortunately there's an easy fix. Just switch the =~ operator to ~ for the second order factors and (with a few other adjustments) you should be all set.

So this:

2ndOrderF1 =~ 1stOrderF1.a + 1stOrderF1.b
2ndOrderF2 =~ 1stOrderF2.a + 1stOrderF2.b
2ndOrderF3 =~ 1stOrderF3.a + 1stOrderF3.b

Becomes:
#Specify 2nd order latents with a loading of 0
#Trick to estimate the model
2ndOrderF1 =~ 0*ind10
2ndOrderF2 =~ 0*ind10
2ndOrderF3 =~ 0*ind10


#Use regression instead of loading operator
1stOrderF1.a ~  1*2ndOrderF1 
1stOrderF1.b ~  2ndOrderF1 
1stOrderF2.a ~ 1*2ndOrderF2 
1stOrderF2.b ~ 2ndOrderF2
1stOrderF3.a ~ 1*2ndOrderF3
1stOrderF3.b ~ 2ndOrderF3

#don't allow 1st order factors to covary (as is default)
1stOrderF1.a ~~ 0*1stOrderF1.b + 0*1stOrderF2.a + 0*1stOrderF2.b + 0*1stOrderF3.a + 0*1stOrderF3.b
1stOrderF1.b ~~ 0*1stOrderF2.a + 0*1stOrderF2.b + 0*1stOrderF3.a + 0*1stOrderF3.b
1stOrderF2.a ~~ 0*1stOrderF2.b + 0*1stOrderF3.a + 0*1stOrderF3.b
1stOrderF2.b ~~ 0*1stOrderF3.a + 0*1stOrderF3.b
1stOrderF3.a ~~ 0*1stOrderF3.b
